Summary  
Data source overview: This ICML paper introduces Conservative Objective Models (COMs), a training and optimisation procedure for fully–offline model-based optimisation (MBO). By learning conservative, lower-bounding estimates of an unknown objective through an adversarial regulariser, COMs prevent the optimiser from moving into out-of-distribution regions where the proxy objective is spuriously high. Theory (Proposition 1) and experiments on seven benchmark tasks show COMs improves performance and stability compared with prior methods.  

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[74] – Medium–high confidence: paper is self-contained, causal flow is explicit, JSON validated by hand. Remaining uncertainty stems from choosing best node granularity and inferring AI-safety-relevant intervention lifecycles.  

Inference-strategy justification: Only light inference (confidence 2) was used where the paper implied but did not explicitly state causal links (e.g. lack of active data exacerbates overestimation). All interventions are directly described and do not rely on speculative leaps.  

Extraction completeness explanation: Every reasoning step from the top-level risk (invalid designs in offline MBO) to the concrete interventions (train COMs with adversarial regularisation, auto-tune conservatism with τ, match ascent steps) is represented. Nodes are decomposed to white-box components (regulariser, adversarial sampling, constrained objective) to maximise merge-ability across 500 k sources. All nodes participate in at least one edge; no isolated subgraphs remain.  

Key limitations:  
1. The paper focuses on design-time optimisation problems; deployment-time safety risks are only indirectly covered.  
2. Hardware and domain-specific implementation details (e.g. protein encodings) were omitted because they do not influence the causal safety fabric.  
3. Lifecycle categorisation for algorithmic interventions is approximate because COMs straddle model-design and training phases.
